draft.title: Two-way tables
card: A two-way table lists the outcomes of one event down the side and the outcomes of a second event across the top. Each cell shows one combined outcome.
Count the cells to find the total number of combined outcomes. A die and a coin give 6 rows × 2 columns = 12 cells.
To find a probability, count the cells that match the event and divide by the total number of cells. This works when every cell is equally likely.
Example: roll a die and toss a coin. Cells with an even number and a head are 2H, 4H and 6H. That is 3 cells, so P(even and head) = 3/12 = 1/4.
draft.remember: Count the matching cells, then divide by the total number of cells.

a.q: A spinner has 4 equal sections and a coin is tossed. A two-way table lists every combined outcome. How many cells does it have?
a.why: The spinner gives 4 rows and the coin gives 2 columns, so 4 × 2 = 8 cells. Adding 4 + 2 = 6 is the tempting mistake, but each spinner result pairs with both coin results.
a.clue: Multiply the rows by the columns.

b.q: Leo rolls a die and tosses a coin. All 12 combined outcomes are equally likely. What is P(a number greater than 4 and a tail)?
b.why: Numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6, so the matching cells are 5T and 6T. That is 2 cells out of 12, so the probability is 2/12. Using 2/6 forgets that the table has 12 cells, not 6.
b.clue: List the matching cells, then divide by all the cells.

check.summary: No problems found. Both intended answers (8 cells, and 2/12) are correct, and the card and explanations are accurate and stay within this point.
